============

Code agents represent a paradigm shift in how artificial intelligence systems interact with programming and software development. Unlike traditional code completion tools, modern code agents possess the ability to understand complex requirements, generate multi-file codebases, execute code iteratively, and debug their own outputs. While the capabilities of code agents have advanced rapidly, significant concerns remain regarding their safety, security, and reliability. Code agents may inadvertently generate malicious code, expose sensitive information, introduce security vulnerabilities, or behave unpredictably in edge cases. The autonomous nature of these agents—capable of executing code and modifying systems—amplifies the potential impact of such failures.

Red-teaming, the practice of systematically probing AI systems for vulnerabilities and unsafe behaviors, has emerged as a critical methodology for ensuring the trustworthiness of AI systems. Traditionally applied to large language models for detecting harmful content generation, red-teaming is now being adapted for the unique challenges posed by code agents. Code-specific red-teaming must address not only text-based safety concerns but also the execution of potentially harmful code, security vulnerabilities in generated software, and the reliable operation of autonomous agents.

This paper provides a comprehensive survey of research advances at the intersection of code agents and red-teaming. We examine the landscape of code agent architectures, review existing red-teaming methodologies, and analyze frameworks specifically designed for code agent evaluation. ==========
